subject: [PATCH 0/3] mm: fixes for THP migration, swap-in and device-private smaps

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo expressed concerns that scanning every page in a folio could be costly, and questioned why we're swapping out folios containing hardware-poisoned pages instead of migrating away from them.
reviews.raw_body:
Hm, isn't scanning every single page in the folio potentially quite costly
here?  I thought the point of batching was to improve performance overall?

It seems broken to have stuff potentially interact with hwpoison but then
to only set the folio-level flag much later?

Also why are we swapping out folios containing hwpoison pages? Shouldn't we
migrate away from the hwpoison? :) (I'm not really familiar with the hw
poison stuff)

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested auditing PMD level device private entries as they have been the source of many issues, and explicitly gave an Acked-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
It feels like PMD level device private entries have been the source of a lot of
issues, maybe a good area to audit in general... :)

Acked-by: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM) <ljs@kernel.org>

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), agreed to restructure in v2.

Author acknowledged the need to check every subpage during swap-in, but expressed concern about the performance cost.

The author addressed Lorenzo's concern about get_hwpoison_page() not being able to get a reference to the subpage when memory_failure() is called, explaining that this is intentional and due to the comment in memory_failure() stating that error handling paths for get_hwpoison_page() are fine. The author also acknowledged that a large folio briefly off the LRU can still be mapped afterwards.

The author is addressing a concern about the error handling when get_hwpoison_page() fails for a folio that is off the LRU, and they agree to add an additional check before checking for hardware-poisoned pages.
reviews.raw_body:
Hello Lorenzo,

Thanks for the reviews!

---

Swapping in requires checking every subpage, so there would be a cost.
I guess trading it off for correctness :(

---

PG_has_hwpoisoned lives in the second page, so memory_failure() only
sets it once it holds a folio reference, otherwise it could race with a
THP split. If get_hwpoison_page() can't get a reference,
memory_failure() gives up with only the subpage marked. The comment
above folio_set_has_hwpoisoned() in memory_failure() says that is fine:

  Don't need care about the above error handling paths for
  get_hwpoison_page() since they handle either free page
  or unhandlable page.

But a large folio that is briefly off the LRU, e.g. isolated by
reclaim, takes those paths too and can still be mapped afterwards.

---

The error hits a folio that is already in the swap
cache, e.g. while reclaim has it off the LRU to write it out, and
get_hwpoison_page() fails for any folio that is off the LRU. Normally
memory_failure() would split the folio and isolate the bad page (for
an uncorrected error there is nothing to migrate; that is soft
offline). Here it does neither, and the folio stays in the swap cache
with only the subpage marked.

While looking at this I also noticed that the fallback drops a freshly
read (not yet anon) folio from the swap cache and frees it with the
poisoned page in it. We should actually actually also check folio_test_anon()
before checking folio_has_any_hwpoisoned_page().

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary:
reviewer suggested replacing a custom function with an existing one from huge_memory.c, specifically recommending the use of page_range_has_hwpoisoned() to avoid code duplication

Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a device-private PMD is split while being accessed by the smaps code, potentially leading to incorrect accounting of private mappings.
reviews.raw_body:
It looks almost the same as page_range_has_hwpoisoned() in mm/huge_memory.c.
Maybe change the function to call page_range_has_hwpoisoned() instead.

---

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-11-11.patch_summary: This patch series addresses three issues in the Linux kernel related to Transparent Huge Pages (THP) migration, swap-in operations, and device-private System Map (smaps). The first fix prevents a folio reference leak when concurrent MADV_DONTNEED operations are performed on a PMD. The second fix ensures that PTE swap-in batching does not map poisoned subpages of a large swap-cache folio. The third fix accounts for device-private PMDs using mapcounts in smaps, providing accurate private memory statistics.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) expressed concern about introducing another helper function to check for hardware poisoning, suggesting instead that existing helpers testing the large-folio bit be reused due to potential races in memory failure code.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah, we don't really want another helper to check for hwpoison.

If we race with concurrent hwpoison, bad luck. The slapped on memory-failure
code is full of races. That needs a proper long-term solution, not more pain to
core-mm.

So let's please try reusing existing helpers that test the large-folio bit.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the 'present' field in smaps_pte_entry() is misleading because it doesn't use pte_present(), and suggested checking for a match with smaps_pte_entry() instead.
reviews.raw_body:
I think I even spelled that out somewhere at some point while touching that code
... or did I fix the smaps_pte_entry() thing at some point?

"present" is a bit misleading in general, because it's not pte_present() ...

Matches smaps_pte_entry()

Acked-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
reviewer noted that the patch's optimization for PTE swap-in batching now incurs a performance cost for all processes, not just those using device-private mappings

reviewer questioned the necessity of scanning for poisoned subpages when PTE batching is disabled, suggesting it be done only in that specific edge case
reviews.raw_body:
(we don't say subpage apparently :)

Yeah but the cost is now paid by literally everybody...

And...

---

...now you're narrowing this cost to literally a vague edge case.

Can we not just do the scan _only in this case_?

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: reviewer expressed frustration that the patch doesn't handle a specific edge case, and suggested that the author should have included it in the original code
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah exactly. See Usama's reply - it really does narrow into a weird edge
case. Scan there if you want to scan at all.

Otherwise tough luck yes.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan found the patch acceptable and provided a Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense.

Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan noted that the comment 'Like what smaps_pte_entry() does' is not a clear review of the patch, but rather an acknowledgement of similarity between two functions.
reviews.raw_body:
Like what smaps_pte_entry() does.
